thread.title: Intel's Reported Bug Hits Chipmaker's Shares, Boosts Rival AMD

title: Intel's Reported Bug Hits Chipmaker's Shares, Boosts Rival AMD
text:
With reports of a potential bug in Intel Corp. ( INTC ) technology, Intel shares fell while those of rival chip maker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. ( AMD ) jumped on Wednesday morning.
AMD spiked 5.7% to $11.61 in morning trading on Wednesday, while Intel dropped 2.4% to $45.74.
The issue exposes so-called kernel memory, which "may contain all sorts of secrets, such as passwords, login keys, files cached from disk, and so on," The Register, a tech website, reports.
"Think of the kernel as God sitting on a cloud, looking down on Earth. It's there, and no normal being can see it, yet they can pray to it," The Register explained. People can also apparently hack it to get at the valuable information stored within the kernel.
According to The Register, the vulnerability requires "a significant redesign" of the kernels in Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ) and Linux operating systems, as well as updates to Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) operating systems. Fixing the problem via a software patch could lead to noticeable slowdowns in computers using Intel's affected chips.
Intel's woes are an unexpected boon for AMD. As TheStreet.com reported Tuesday, AMD faces a rocky competitive environment in early 2018 because of new offerings from Intel and Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) . Shares of Nvidia gained about 4% in morning trading Wednesday to $207.65.
While Intel has gained 28% over the last 52 weeks, AMD is down 3.9%. Meanwhile, Nvidia is up 95% over the period.
Intel did not immediately respond to a query for this story.
